source.title: From Concept Alignment to Causal Grounding: An Intervention Test of Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness
source.authors: Qianli Wang; Yi-Long Wang; Dennis Wei; Jing-Yi Sun; Simon Ostermann; Isabelle Augenstein; Pepa Atanasova; Nils Feldhus

record.tranche_reason: Applies an SAE-based feature analysis to five LLMs and reports measurements and interventions on SAE features, bearing indirectly on V4. It does not test the original toy-network superposition claim.
record.gate_note: The paper uses sparse autoencoders to identify active latent features in LLM residual streams, measures overlap between prediction and CoT passes, and ablates shared features. It describes SAE latents as concepts but does not measure superposition geometry, feature sparsity in the original sense, or neurons’ polysemanticity. SAE configuration comparisons and qualitative feature descriptions are not evidence that SAE features are complete canonical units.
record.test_reason: The study uses off-the-shelf SAEs (Llama-, Gemma-, Qwen-Scope) to measure CoT faithfulness. It assumes SAE latents are near-monosemantic concepts. Every Δp result scores its own faithfulness metric: how much answer probability drops when features shared between the prediction and CoT passes are ablated. No result asks whether features are superposed, spread across neurons, recoverable by a dictionary in the V4 sense, canonical (V5), or one-dimensional (V6). The reader's T3/'tests V4' guess is therefore wrong. Causal relevance of SAE latents to answers is a property of the authors' method, not evidence on the claim.
record.authors_conclusion:
Mostly correct, but the clause 'not as evidence about superposition geometry' is the reader's framing; the authors don't discuss superposition beyond a footnote. The authors conclude several things:
- Correlational concept-alignment metrics are high, but only weakly track causal effect (lift 1.08).
- Δp, validated against random, norm-matched and SAE-configuration controls, is needed to assess faithfulness.
- Faithfulness peaks at mid-to-late layers. It is distributed in Qwen3 but localized in Llama-3.1-8B.
- Scale reshapes the layer profile.
- Causally important shared concepts are not always verbalized in the CoT.
record.recipe_differences: Uses pretrained SAEs to compare LLM prediction and CoT activations, then ablates shared features and measures answer-probability change; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that Δp varies substantially by layer, model architecture, model scale, and dataset. SAE width and sparsity also produce some variation, although the authors report broadly similar profiles across configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE reconstruction FVU for Qwen3-1.7B on LogiQA ranges 0.01–0.18 across layers, below 0.1 for most layers (Fig. 21, App. I.3). This is a sanity check on the off-the-shelf SAE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Off-the-shelf residual-stream SAEs reconstruct most activation variance in a mid-size LLM (weak, single-model evidence related to V4's dictionary-recovery part).

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-wise Δp correlates highly across SAE width/ℓ0 configurations (Pearson r ≈0.8–0.96, Tables 20–23). CC-SAE and Jaccard correlate only moderately (≈0.38–0.93), with Jaccard most sensitive to sparsity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream SAE-based metrics are fairly robust to dictionary width/sparsity, while feature-set overlap measures are configuration-sensitive (related to, but not a test of, V5 stability).

record.problems: The paper notes there is no ground-truth metric for CoT faithfulness and treats its measures as proxies. The analysis conditions on cases where CoT and no-CoT predictions agree. It uses off-the-shelf SAEs and tests a limited set of models and reasoning datasets; causal feature effects do not establish that SAE features are complete or canonical units.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was reached. Omitted Table 10 and Table 13 controls B and C, top-k comparisons, and other control conditions; omitted Tables 4 and 5 feature-count/overlap and peak/average results, plus the SAE-configuration, sufficiency, and reconstruction analyses. These are not evidence about the toy superposition versions; several are related methodological robustness results.

untested.parts: All: no toy networks, no geometry, no sparsity-dependent transition.
All: no capacity or importance analysis of neurons.
All: no analysis of causes of polysemantic neurons.

Whether features spread across many neurons, and whether LLMs contain sparse features an SAE recovers. SAEs are used off the shelf and assumed to recover concepts; only an FVU sanity check for one model is reported.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features. The width/sparsity ablation compares Δp profiles across configurations, not feature identity.
All: no test of feature dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'tests' (T3) to 'uses_without_test' (T4); SAEs serve purely as a measurement tool for CoT faithfulness. The text says sparsity 'pushes these concepts toward monosemanticity rather than superposition', which assumes the claim rather than testing it. The only superposition mention is footnote 7, which speculates about 'higher superposition density' in middle layers without measuring it. All 60 rows relinked to 'none'. No verdicts given.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, overcomplete sparse feature storage, near-orthogonal directions, and sparsity-dependent geometric transitions.
Whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity or makes important features dedicated and others shared.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
The study tests SAE feature activations and their causal contribution in LLMs; it does not test feature spreading across neurons or establish general SAE recovery across models and tasks.
The study varies SAE configuration and reports robustness of some aggregate metrics, but does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of model representation.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

reader_labels.reason: Ablating SAE features shared between passes reduces answer probability across the reported model-dataset settings; random-feature controls have much smaller effects. This is indirect evidence for causally relevant SAE features in these LLMs, not a test of neuron-level feature spreading. Rows D1–D15, C1–C15, A1–A15, B1–B15.
